methods.name: syns.repo
methods.description: The Syns repository of this session's folder, or the placed folder it is, and its head version. The method a page polls with watch: one cheap call.

version.description: The head. null for a repository with no commit yet.

number.description: The head as a number, for display. Present where the CLI reports it: CLI 0.3.6 and later.

holder.description: In a placed folder: OWNER/NAME of the repository holding it. owner, name, role, visibility and fileCount are then the holder's.

path.description: In a placed folder: its path in the holder. Every path a page uses is counted from it.

sharedFolder.description: true in a folder-only collaborator's checkout of a shared folder: the record is the folder's identity, and fileCount is 0.

no_repo.description: The session's folder holds no Syns repository, or the caller is the home page.

no_access.description: The machine's account cannot reach the repository, or is logged out.

cli_missing.description: No syns on that machine; an operator installs it or names it in the plugin's settings.

timeout.description: The CLI did not answer in time. Retry a read; after a write, re-read syns.repo first.

folder_out_of_place.description: A placed folder stands away from the path its identity file records; an operator moves it back.

bad_scope.description: The scope is not a placed folder of the session's own repository, or the CLI does not act there: a folder action at a root, a holder action in a placed folder, a folder's people before it is shared.

**Tool first.** Asked for a piece of work the person will keep working in? Look for a template first: `syns explore -t syns-app -q <words>`, then follow `syns cat TOOLS.md --repo bartsoj/syns-templates`.

**Syns repository.** When this session's folder is a Syns repository, or a folder placed in one, the page reads and writes it through `syns.*`. Not in `context.get`, or `unavailable` / `no_repo`: say so and keep the rest working; never show invented data.

- **The page names no repository:** it sees the one, or the placed folder, its session's folder belongs to; paths count from there.
- **Pages show pushed state:** your edits reach the page after your turn is pushed.
- **Every write needs `base`,** the `version` last read from `syns.repo`. On `stale_head`, re-read and let the reader retry; on `checkout_dirty` an agent is mid-turn: retry when `version` moves.
- **Load with `syns.ls` and `syns.readMany`;** poll only `syns.repo` with `watch`. Writes and shares act at once: only from a control saying what changes, for whom.

Every method: the page guide (its command is in your page instruction's *More*), section *Capabilities from contributors*. Installing or diagnosing the plugin: `syns cat SETUP.md --repo bartsoj/syns-bb-plugin-setup`.
guide:
# Syns: the session's repository, from a page

## When this applies

Only when the session's folder is a Syns repository, or a folder placed in one. At load, look for `syns.repo` in `context.get` and call it. Absent, or `unavailable` / `no_repo`: say so on the page and keep the rest working. The page never names a repository, session or folder. Never show invented data in its place.

## A placed folder

A folder placed in a repository (a tool) is all the page sees: every `path` is counted from it; nothing outside is reachable. A document may also set a scope (`threadPage.setScope`): a placed folder of the session's own repository, holding its own identity file; its calls then answer for that folder alone. `bad_scope` refuses anything else: a plain folder, one below a placed folder, another checkout, a folder outside the session's, or any scope where the session's folder is no Syns repository. `syns.repo` adds `holder` (OWNER/NAME) and `path`: show those. `owner`, `name`, `role`, `visibility` and `fileCount` are the holder's; build no path or link from them. `version` is the holder's head, so `syns.diff` may list nothing. Once the CLI checks writes against the folder only, a write is `stale_head` only when the folder changed after `base`; before, any change to the holder. Writes publish to all who share the holder. `syns.place { template, path }` places a template as a new folder, always at the session's folder.

## Versions

`version` is a commit id, opaque: compare it, pass it back, show it to nobody. `number` is the same version for display. `blob` changes exactly when a file's content does.

## Loading a wiki

1. `syns.ls { recursive: true }`: every file with its `blob`, and the `version` listed. `truncated: true` means incomplete: list folder by folder.
2. `syns.readMany { paths, version }` in groups of up to 64, passing that `version`; follow `deferred` the same way. `too_large` carries `size` (the bound counts the text as JSON escapes it): read it with `syns.read`.

300 files: one `syns.ls` and about five `syns.readMany`, inside the shared 120 calls a minute. A `syns.read` window's lines are joined with `\n`, without `\r` or a final newline: to write a file back exactly, read it with `syns.readMany`.

## Staying current

Poll only `syns.repo`, with the host's `watch`. When its `version` differs from the one held, `syns.diff { from }` lists each changed path and `status` up to `to.version`; re-read those at `to.version`. There is no push.

`syns.history` says who changed what. A page's write has `by.integration` `syns-pages` and `by.trigger` `page`; then `by.run` is the session whose page made it. Others set `by.run` too: never read it alone as a page's. `syns.revert` records none.

## Writing

Every file write but `syns.revert` carries `base`, the `version` last read; the returned `version` is the next `base`. A new file: `syns.write` with `create: true`, which refuses rather than overwrite. `changed: 0`: nothing differed, or the path was gone; no version made. A request past a method's bound comes back from the bridge as `invalid_response`: split it. `syns.revert` has no stale check and no provenance: call `syns.repo` just before offering it, and say what it overwrites. A picture larger than 720 KiB goes in ordered pieces; `bad_offset`: send from `detail.expected`. Beside texts in one version: `hold: true`, then its `upload` in `syns.commit`.

## Sharing and people

Each method acts where the CLI acts, in the page's own scope. In a placed folder: `syns.shareInfo`, `syns.share`, `syns.unshare`, `syns.folderVisibility`, `syns.enableChecks`. At a repository's root: `syns.repoVisibility`. The collaborator methods act on the scope's people: in a shared placed folder its own (CLI 0.3.14; until shared, `bad_scope` saying to share first; older CLIs, `bad_scope`); at a root the **whole repository's**, so never offer root people for one folder. Elsewhere the CLI refuses: `bad_scope`; show controls only where they apply (`syns.repo`'s `holder`, `syns.shareInfo`'s `shared`). `syns.collaboratorRole` and `syns.collaboratorRemove` take the `user.id` that `syns.collaborators` answers; find someone with `syns.users`. Roles are the CLI's; a shared folder takes `read` or `write`.

They act at once, with no dialog, and reach other people. So:

- **Only from a control the reader presses for that action:** never on load, from a timer or `watch`, or chained after another call.
- **The control shows who gets what** before it is pressed: the person and the role, or everyone the folder reaches. `admin` can also share, change visibility and manage people: say so.
- **Public is labelled apart:** "anyone, signed in or not, can find and read this". Never a default; never one option in a list beside private. A public name beginning with a private holder's name shows that name: say so first.
- **`syns.unshare`** removes everyone who reached the folder through it; its name stays reserved.

Poll none of these with `watch`. Errors come back from the CLI: a refusal with no reason carries the CLI's own words as `message`.

## Every method

The host's roster above (*Registered now*) gives each method's effect, bounds, description and every reason it may answer. `path` is counted from the repository's root, or the placed folder, with `/` separators, at most 1,024 characters; no leading `/` or `-`, no `\` or control character, no `.` or `..` segment. A `?` marks an optional key; a bare `version` or `path` key has that type; no other key is accepted. `…collaborator` is `{ user?: { id: string, username?: string|null, name?: string|null, email?: string|null, image?: string|null }, role?: string, createdAt?: string|null }`. `…record` is `{ owner?: string, name?: string, visibility?: string, role?: string|null, sharedFolder?: bool, status?: string, description?: string|null, heldIn?: { owner?: string, name?: string, path?: string }|null }`.

### `syns.repo`
- Params: `{}`
- Result: `{ owner: string, name: string, version: version|null, number?: int|null, role: string|null, visibility: string, fileCount: int, holder?: string, path?: string, sharedFolder?: bool }`

### `syns.whoami`
- Params: `{}`
- Result: `{ id: string, username: string, emailVerified: bool|null, name: string|null, email: string|null, image: string|null, bio: string|null, company: string|null, location: string|null, pronouns: string|null, timeZone: string|null, createdAt: string|null, updatedAt: string|null }`

### `syns.ls`
- Params: `{ path?, recursive?: bool, version?, offset?: int(0–…), limit?: int(1–1500) }`
- Result: `{ version, number: int, truncated: bool, total: int, nextOffset: int|null, entries: [{ path: string, type: "file"|"dir", size: int|null, blob: string|null }] }`

### `syns.readMany`
- Params: `{ paths: [path] (1–64), version? }`
- Result: `{ version, files: [{ path: string, text?: string, size?: int, blob?: string|null, error?: "not_found"|"too_large"|"not_text" }], deferred: [string] }`

### `syns.history`
- Params: `{ path?, limit?: int(1–100) }`
- Result: `{ total: int, entries: [{ version, number: int, parent: version|null, author: string|null, at: string, message: string, paths: [string] (0–200), pathsTruncated: bool, by: { integration: string|null, run: string|null, trigger: string|null } }] }`

### `syns.commit`
- Params: `{ base: version, message?: string(≤500), files?: [{ path, text?: string(≤1048576), base64?: string(≤983040), upload?: string(≤64) }] (0–64), deletions?: [path] (0–64) }`
- Result: `{ version, number: int, changed: int }`

### `syns.read`
- Params: `{ path, version?, offset?: int(1–…), limit?: int(1–5000), fit?: bool }`
- Result: `{ version, number: int, path: string, text: string, offset: int, limit: int, totalLines: int, size: int, blob: string }`

### `syns.glob`
- Params: `{ pattern: string(≤512), path?, version?, offset?: int(0–…), limit?: int(1–2000) }`
- Result: `{ version, number: int, truncated: bool, total: int, nextOffset: int|null, matches: [{ path: string, size: int, blob: string }] }`

### `syns.grep`
- Params: `{ pattern: string(≤512), path?, glob?: [string(≤512)] (0–8), ignoreCase?: bool, context?: int(0–10), output?: "content"|"files"|"count", headLimit?: int(1–1000), version? }`
- Result: `{ version, number: int, output: "content"|"files"|"count", truncated: bool, skipped: [{ path: string, reason: string }], matches?: [{ path: string, line: int, text: string, context: [{ line: int, text: string }] }], files?: [string], counts?: [{ path: string, count: int }] }`

### `syns.diff`
- Params: `{ from: version, to?: version, patch?: bool }`
- Result: `{ from: { version, number: int }, to: { version, number: int }, files: [{ path: string, status: string, patch?: string }] }`

### `syns.write`
- Params: `{ path, text: string(≤1048576), base: version, message?: string(≤500), create?: bool }`
- Result: `{ version, number: int }`

### `syns.edit`
- Params: `{ path, old: string(≤32768), new: string(≤32768), replaceAll?: bool, base: version, message?: string(≤500) }`
- Result: `{ version, number: int, changed: int }`

### `syns.rm`
- Params: `{ path, base: version, message?: string(≤500) }`
- Result: `{ version, number: int, changed: int }`

### `syns.revert`
- Params: `{ path, to: version, message?: string(≤500) }`
- Result: `{ version, number: int }`

### `syns.readBinary`
- Params: `{ path, version?, offset?: int(0–26214400) }`
- Result: `{ version, number: int, path: string, size: int, blob: string, mediaType: string|null, sha256: string(≤64), offset: int, base64: string, nextOffset: int|null }`

### `syns.writeBinary`
- Params: `{ path, base64: string(≤983040), base: version, message?: string(≤500), offset?: int(0–26214400), size?: int(0–52428800), sha256?: string(≤64), hold?: bool }`
- Result: `{ complete: bool, received: int, version?, number?: int, changed?: int, upload?: string(≤64) }`

### `syns.place`
- Params: `{ template: string(≤201), path, version?: int(1–…) }`
- Result: `{ path: string, holder: string, template: { repo: string, version: int, sha: string }, version, number: int, checks: [string], enableChecks: string|null }`

### `syns.shareInfo`
- Params: `{}`
- Result: `{ …record, holder: string, path: string, holderRole?: string|null, shared: bool, offeredName?: string }`

### `syns.share`
- Params: `{ name?: string(≤100) }`
- Result: `{ …record, holder: string, path: string, created: bool }`

### `syns.unshare`
- Params: `{}`
- Result: `{ owner: string, name: string, holder: string, path: string, unshared: bool, retired?: bool|null }`

### `syns.folderVisibility`
- Params: `{ visibility: "public"|"private", name?: string(≤100) }`
- Result: `{ …record, holder: string, path: string, created?: bool }`

### `syns.repoVisibility`
- Params: `{ visibility: "public"|"private" }`
- Result: `{ …record }`

### `syns.collaborators`
- Params: `{ limit?: int(1–100), offset?: int(0–…) }`
- Result: `{ total: int, limit?: int, offset?: int, data: [{ …collaborator }] }`

### `syns.collaboratorAdd`
- Params: `{ user: string(≤320), role: "admin"|"write"|"read" }`
- Result: `{ added: bool, target: string, role: string }`

### `syns.collaboratorRole`
- Params: `{ id: string(≤128), role: "admin"|"write"|"read" }`
- Result: `{ …collaborator }`

### `syns.collaboratorRemove`
- Params: `{ id: string(≤128) }`
- Result: `{ removed: bool, userId: string }`

### `syns.enableChecks`
- Params: `{}`
- Result: `{ holder: string, path: string, enabled: [string], version?, number?: int }`

### `syns.explore`
- Params: `{ query?: string(≤200), tags?: [string(≤100)] (0–8), status?: "active"|"draft"|"completed"|"abandoned", limit?: int(1–100), offset?: int(0–…) }`
- Result: `{ total: int, limit?: int, offset?: int, data: [{ owner: string, name: string, description?: string|null, tags?: [string], status?: string|null, visibility?: string, fileCount?: int, forkCount?: int, updatedAt?: string|null }] }`

### `syns.users`
- Params: `{ query: string(≤100), limit?: int(1–100) }`
- Result: `{ data: [{ id: string, username: string, name?: string|null, image?: string|null }] }`

## Errors

Branch on `reason` when there is one, else on `code`: `conflict` means re-read, `unavailable` means not now or not here, `not_found` means it is not there. `message` may be shown to the reader.

- `unavailable` / `no_repo` — The session's folder holds no Syns repository, or the caller is the home page.
- `unavailable` / `no_access` — The machine's account cannot reach the repository, or is logged out.
- `unavailable` / `cli_missing` — No syns on that machine; an operator installs it or names it in the plugin's settings.
- `unavailable` / `timeout` — The CLI did not answer in time. Retry a read; after a write, re-read syns.repo first.
- `unavailable` / `folder_out_of_place` — A placed folder stands away from the path its identity file records; an operator moves it back.
- `invalid_params` / `bad_scope` — The scope is not a placed folder of the session's own repository, or the CLI does not act there: a folder action at a root, a holder action in a placed folder, a folder's people before it is shared.
- `unavailable` / `not_logged_in` — No Syns login on that machine.
- `unavailable` / `folder_write_unsupported` — The server is too old for writes in a placed folder. Nothing written; reads work.
- `conflict` / `stale_head` — The repository, or placed folder, changed after base; nothing written; detail.current is the head. Re-read, show what changed, never retry blindly.
- `conflict` / `checkout_dirty` — The session's folder has unpublished edits, usually its agent mid-turn. Nothing written; retry when syns.repo's version moves.
- `invalid_params` / `invalid_change` — A path named twice across files and deletions, or no change at all.
- `conflict` / `bad_offset` — Send the piece at detail.expected; 0 means start again (pieces or an upload are dropped after a minute).
- `invalid_params` / `bad_pattern` — The regular expression or glob does not parse.
- `conflict` / `exists` — create was set and the path exists at base.
- `invalid_params` / `no_match` — old occurs nowhere in the file.
- `invalid_params` / `many_matches` — old occurs detail.count times and replaceAll is not set.
- `invalid_params` / `bad_hash` — The gathered bytes do not match sha256; nothing published.
- `invalid_params` / `too_large` — Past detail.max bytes, the most one file may hold (25 MiB).
- `unavailable` / `cli_too_old` — The machine's syns is older than detail.need (detail.have): syns upgrade there.
- `conflict` / `occupied` — path already holds a file at the head or on disk; choose another.
- `not_found` / `no_such_template` — template is no repository the reader can read.
- `unavailable` / `not_permitted` — Syns answered 403 for this account: a role too low for it, or a server limit. The CLI says no more.
- `invalid_params` / `bad_name` — name breaks the repository-name rule.
- `conflict` / `name_taken` — Another repository holds name; offer the reader another.
- `not_found` / `no_such_user` — user names nobody on Syns.
- `conflict` / `already_collaborator` — user already holds a grant here; nothing changed.
- `not_found` — the path, the `version`, or what was named does not exist.
- `invalid_params` — the parameters do not fit the method; fix the page.
- `response_too_large` — ask for less.
- `handler_error` — anything else; `message` holds the CLI's own words when it gave some.

## What a page cannot do here

Choose a repository, or reach outside its scope. Read unpublished edits. Write a file without a `base`, but for `syns.revert`. Set a commit's provenance. Run any CLI command but the ones behind these methods: no login, upgrade, push, pull, sync, delete or fork.
